summary:
We proposed a new name for this point and location in Noctis Labyrinthus: 
"Noctis Tree" (NT). Zone/Mission: "Under the NT".

Additionally, we mapped out a route to explore the terrain, starting from two points identified by NASA (STAGE 1).

Next, we move to STAGE 2: Under The Noctis Tree. 
Phase 1: consists of studying Noctis Mons. 
Phase 2: focuses on analyzing an area selected by our team—a specific passage within Noctis Labyrinthus, located to the south in a zone we have named "Under the Noctis Tree" (a name we also proposed for the rock formation as part of this project). Studying this passage could serve as a model for the *chasmas* (canyons) that make up the vast network extending westward toward the Tharsis region, allowing for an analysis of conditions that might support future habitability. This phase is designated as "NOCTIS THROUGH."
Phase 3 then picks up from the "Under the Noctis Tree" route and continues westward.

For this mission, the plan involves deploying a prototype exploration vehicle—a CAT-ROVER, "climbing rover"—which will drop off the astronauts at the NASA research base located at the Relict Glacier. Subsequently, the rover will venture into the Noctis volcano ("Noctis Mons") to conduct its study, and then it descends through the designated area to fulfill the objectives of the "Noctis Through" phase and complete the study mission.
details:
1. To represent the route, we used a map of the chosen area—sourced from a NASA database as a foundation.
We considered  topographic, geophysical, atmospheric and spectral data from various sources to created a clay model to physically represent the proposed route. This was a highly beneficial activity for the child, who is a future astronaut on this team.

Then, frame-by-frame animation—using the stop-motion technique—was employed to create the impression of movement along the chosen route.

2. NEW NAME
Noctis Tree

We are giving a new name to a rock formation whose silhouette could serve as a visual landmark from space—and as an icon and symbol of the beginning of a new life, a new home, and a new Earth on Mars.

We have named the chosen area "under the Noctis Tree," which gives its name to the proposed mission and the project.

2 NEW ROVER, NEW PATH

Mission Under the Noctis Tree

SCIENTIFIC OBJECTIVE
A route toward a new mission—situated " "Under the Noctis Tree"—is proposed, with the aim of testing the terrain, habitability conditions, and the potential for future life on Mars. This section of the labyrinth will be used as a sample.

https://science.nasa.gov/resource/curiositys-proposed-path-up-mount-sharp/

We have designed a special route for a prototype "escalator rover"—named by the team as the "CCR39 Cutu Cat-rover"—a name derived from its technical characteristics, with "39" representing the current Martian year. This highly resilient prototype features "9-lives" shielding, HD night-vision cameras, multiple sensors, and feline-like agility—complete with claws.

In this way, it will be possible to shorten the journey—a shortcut to other paths—to study the area in the field, including labyrinths that previous rovers have not explored.

And to precede the human team into the area, studying and establishing the conditions for habitability in the designated zone. With the goal of conducting field research in the deep reaches of the Noctis Labyrinth.



AREA SELECTED FOR PHASE 2 STUDY This route would constitute a "Phase 2"—following the NASA-planned "Phase 1" mission at the Noctis landing site—and would involve studying the glacier located at the foot of the inactive shield volcano, Noctis Mons. The objective is to study this passage and, using this sector as a reference, determine characteristics shared with the other deep canyons within the labyrinthine terrain. These labyrinthine structures offer significant potential for studying mists, microclimates, and soil. They provide natural protection against high levels of atmospheric radiation, Martian winds, and meteorite impacts. Furthermore, they may harbor a more favorable microclimate. According to recent studies, this area is located relatively close to a potential water source—a relict glacier at the base of the inactive shield volcano, Noctis Mons. It is necessary to investigate these factors, as well as to analyze risks such as rockfalls and low atmospheric pressure. Other key data points to examine include morning mists and the saline composition of the soil, which may point to past water activity (as has been detected in other sectors of the Noctis region).
